pr_title: sql, backupccl: new databases have public schemas backed by descriptors
pr_body:
Various backup restore changes resulting from changes to public schema having a descriptor.

Notably work has been done to create a public schema with a descriptor during restore when the backup is from an older version where public schemas are not backed by descriptors.

Remove hardcoded cases where public schema is synthetic.

Generally support UDS for backup/restore.

@cockroachdb/bulk-io please review the last 2 commits.

Fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/72433
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/72000)

Thanks for the reviews, super appreciated on this one.

Going for the merge 🤞

bors r+

issue_context.title: sql: create public schemas backed by descriptors for new databases
issue_context.body:
Issue for: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/72000

Before we do https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/55793 we need to actually create public schemas with descriptors for new databases.

Additionally we'll have to synthesize a new public schema descriptor for databases restored with virtual public schemas

Epic CRDB-1521

review_comments: We are overwriting any other Schemas that might have been already written in `rewriteDatabaseDescs`. I don't think this is correct.

This was incorrect but in a different way because we only do this if `db.Schemas == nil`

Gonna add a test in `restore_old_versions` to make sure this works when we restore a database with a UDS and a synthetic public schema

This does not seem correct. We are iterating over all schema objects that are being restored, and if they are in the database for which we synthesized a public schema descriptor, we are rewriting the parent schema ID to public? Doesn't this put everything in the public schema?
Can we be more selective about only setting the `ParentSchemaID` field for types, tables, and sequences, if they were previously mapped to the `PublicSchemaIDForBackup?
To be clear, this changed from 53 to 54?
53 to 56 I believe. Previously `keys.MinNonPredefinedUserDescID` was 52, which made `DefaultCSVParentID` 52 now its 54.
thanks!
Do we need to `DROP TABLE newbackup.bank`?
Don't need to since we drop the database right afterwards
ditto DROP comment.
Don't need to since we drop the database
can you explain why all alters have changed to create table as?

Ah it's because we disable moving tables from database to database even if they're in the public schema now due to public schema being a regular schema. It was previously allowed as a special case but now generally disallowed in sql.
ahaa got it, thanks!

Maybe I'm being pedantic but can we check the public desc ID before restore for the database test, and then check that the parentSchemaID of the table is that. I would assume the SELECT wouldnt work if this was busted but 🤷 if you don't mind.

Added

```
row = sqlDB.QueryRow(t, `SELECT id FROM system.namespace WHERE name='test' AND "parentID"=0`)
var parentDBID int
row.Scan(&parentDBID)

row = sqlDB.QueryRow(t, fmt.Sprintf(`SELECT id FROM system.namespace WHERE name='public' AND "parentID"=%d`, parentDBID))
row.Scan(&publicSchemaID)

if publicSchemaID == keys.PublicSchemaID || publicSchemaID == int(descpb.InvalidID) {
	t.Errorf(fmt.Sprintf("expected public schema id to not be %d or %d, found %d", keys.PublicSchemaID, descpb.InvalidID, publicSchemaID))
}
```
